title: Heavenly inheritances: the greatest masters' last words
by: Dev (local model), checked by the writing room

items.text: A figure in white jade robes sits on a lotus of stone, untouched by a single grain of dust. "Ten thousand years I ruled a heaven that is gone. All I kept was the body that ruled it. Take it -- and stand where nothing can move you."

A figure in white jade robes sits on a lotus of stone, untouched by a single grain of dust. "Ten thousand years I ruled a heaven that is gone. All I kept was the body that ruled it. Take it -- and stand where nothing can move you."
There is a seated sage here, and also there isn't: the outline flickers like heat over stone. "I breathed in the void and it did not end me. Breathe as I did, and the heavens will pour into you."

"I breathed in the void and it did not end me. Breathe as I did, and the heavens will pour into you."

Not bones -- a figure of grey metal and jade, seated, its chest open on a single dark seed that still pulses.

"We made the swarm to carry people up the road. Then we forgot why. You remember. Take the seed."
